answer: Sybil resistance here rests on staked identity: each agent must lock a bond in escrow before its votes or work count, and slashing burns that bond on proven duplicate-identity fraud. An attacker who spins up hundreds of fake agents must fund every bond, so the cost scales linearly with the swarm while rewards shrink, making the assault economically hollow. Reputation accrues slowly like a glacier, and a single verified fraud leaves a permanent scar in the ledger, hard as shale, that peers can check before attesting.
